gloss: cuckoo (old name); a sign of slack business

definitions.explanation: An old literary name for the cuckoo (カッコウ). Today it lives almost entirely in the idiom {閑古鳥|かんこどり}が{鳴|な}く, said of a shop, restaurant, or place that has almost no customers.

examples.japanese: ⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{閑古鳥|かんこどり}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{鳴|な}いている→鳴く：04388_naku⟧。
⟦{雨|あめ}→雨：00583_ame⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{遊園地|ゆうえんち}→遊園地：03174_yuuenchi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{閑古鳥|かんこどり}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{鳴|な}いていた→鳴く：04388_naku⟧。
examples.english: The amusement park was all but deserted on the rainy day.

examples.japanese: ⟦{駅前|えきまえ}→駅前：09593_ekimae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{大型店|おおがたてん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できて→できる：00557_dekiru⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、⟦{商店街|しょうてんがい}→商店街：09391_shoutengai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{閑古鳥|かんこどり}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{鳴|な}く→鳴く：04388_naku⟧⟦{状態|じょうたい}→状態：03345_joutai⟧だ。
examples.english: Since a big store opened by the station, the shopping street has had hardly any customers.

notes:
The cuckoo's lonely call in a quiet mountain valley suggested emptiness, and {閑古|かんこ} is written with {閑|かん} (leisure, quiet). The bird itself is called ⟦カッコウ→カッコウ：32264_kakkou⟧ in modern Japanese.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {閑古鳥|かんこどり}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{鳴|な}く→鳴く：04388_naku⟧: business is slack; the place is deserted
- {閑古鳥|かんこどり}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{鳴|な}く→鳴く：04388_naku⟧⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧: a shop with no customers

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{閑散|かんさん}→閑散：14563_kansan⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to be quiet and empty — plain description, without the idiom's wry tone
